newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Benefun seen in HK$100-115 mln IPO - sources.
newsitem.headline: HK's Benefun seen in HK$100-115 mln IPO - sources.

text.p: Fashion products retailer Benefun International Holdings Ltd is expected to issue 100 million shares at a price ranging from HK$1.00 to HK$1.15 each in an initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong, corporate finance sources said.
The sources said the issue price would represent a prospective price/earnings multiple of seven to eight times.
About 90 percent of the issue is for the public subscription and the balance is expected to offer to the company's employees on a preferential basis, they said.
Natwest Markets Corporate Finance Asia Ltd is the sponsor of the issue, sources said.
The IPO is expected to run from May 20 to 27 and dealing in the company shares is expected to begin on June 3.
"The company forecast its profit to reach HK$53 million for the year ending in June 1997 on a turnover of about HK$600 million," said an analyst who attended a company presentation on Monday.

The company posted a turnover of HK$550 million for the year ended in June 1996, up from HK$500 million in 1995 and HK$375 million in 1994. Its net profit also rose to HK$37.5 million in 1996, from HK$32.5 million in 1995 and HK$27.5 million in 1994.

Benefun, which plans to seek a dual listing in Hong Kong and Singapore later in May, is the holding company of Benefashion Ltd, a company which imports and retails a wide range of men's, ladies', and children's casual wear of Benetton S.p.A. under the Benetton, Sisley, 012 and Zerodonto of Benetton brandnames in Hong Kong and Nenetton and 012 apparel in Taiwan.
Last month, garment manufacturer and retailer Heshe Holdings Ltd said it planned to seek a primary listing for its subsidiary Benefun in Hong Kong and secondary listing in Singapore.
